questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

It is not possible to discuss anything with her because of her angry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1, i.e., because of her angry.**

The sentence uses the __incorrect adjective form__ **'angry**', which must be used along with some other noun, such as angry man etc.

Given the context of the sentence, which directly refers to it, __the word should be present in its noun form__, viz., **anger**.

Thus, the rectified sentence is: It is not possible to discuss anything with her **because of her anger.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Every book __is wrote__ by Ruskin Bond is a masterpiece.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"written". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The original sentence, **"Every book is wrote by Ruskin Bond is a masterpiece," **is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The verb **"wrote" **is in the past tense, but it should be in the present tense to agree with the subject **"Every book."**
 
• Option 3, "written," is the correct answer.
 
 
• It is the past participle of the verb "write," and it can be used as an adjective to describe a noun.
 
• In this case, it is used to describe the noun "book."
 
 
 
• Therefore, the best way to improve the sentence is to replace the underlined segment with "written."
 
• The corrected sentence is: Every book written by Ruskin Bond is a masterpiece.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank and make a meaningful sentence.**

The Middle-East job market has always been a _______ destination for Indians.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2, i.e., lucrative.**

The sentence suggests that the __blank must contain an adjective that is appropriate for the noun 'Middle-Eastern job market'.__

Now, job markets cannot be costly, wealthy or luxury. __They signify opportunities which attract__, which is only reflected by '**lucrative**'.

Thus, the completed sentence is: The Middle-East job market has always been a lucrative destination for Indians.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Kaira has upset with me since the accident.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Kaira has upset". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence does not give the contextual meaning. 
 
• This sentence will be in passive form. Here been will be used after has. 
 
• Auxiliary verb, **has**, here, should be used with the past participle form of 'to be__', viz, **has been upset** (if using present perfect tense).
 
• Other correct verbs here would be simple present **'is upset**' or simple past tense verb '**was upset'**.
 
• The correct sentence is: Kaira has been upset with me since the accident. 

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 2". **

questions.question: Five girls took part in a race. Rajni ﬁnished before Mahika but behind Garima. Ashmita ﬁnished before Sanchali but behind Mahika. Who came second in the race?
questions.solution:
1. Five girls took part in a race.

2. Rajni ﬁnished before Mahika but behind Garima.

Garima > Rajni > Mahika

3. Ashmita ﬁnished before Sanchali but behind Mahika.

Mahika > Ashmita > Sanchali

Combining (2) and (3), we get:

Garima > Rajni > Mahika > Ashmita > Sanchali

Hence, ‘Rajni’ came second in the race.

questions.question:
Which two numbers need to be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

72 × 9 + 27 ÷ 3 - 6 = 213
questions.solution:
Given equation: 72 × 9 + 27 ÷ 3 - 6 = 213

1. 9, 6

After interchanging ‘9 and 6’, we get:

L.H.S = 72 × 6 + 27 ÷ 3 – 9

= 432 + 9 – 9

= 432 ≠ R.H.S

**2. 9, 3**

**After interchanging ‘9 and 3’, we get:**

**L.H.S = 72 × 3 + 27 ÷ 9– 6**

**= 216 + 3 – 6**

**= 219 – 6**

**= 213 = R.H.S**

3. 72, 6

After interchanging ‘72 and 6’, we get:

L.H.S = 6 × 9 + 27 ÷ 3 –72

= 54 + 9 – 72

= 63 – 72

= -9 ≠ R.H.S

4. 72, 27

After interchanging ‘72 and 27’, we get:

L.H.S = 27 × 9 + 72 ÷ 3 - 6

= 243 + 24 – 6

= 267 – 6

= 261 ≠ R.H.S

Hence, ‘9, 3’ is the correct answer

questions.question: A car travels for 6 hours at different speeds. For the first two hours at 60 m/s, for the next 2 hours at 50 m/s and for the remaining time at x m/s. If the average speed for the entire journey is 52 m/s, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal time intervals (2 hours each), the average speed over the entire journey is simply the arithmetic mean of the individual speeds.

⇒ Average Speed = (S₁ + S₂ + S₃) ÷ 3

⇒ 52 = (60 + 50 + x) ÷ 3

⇒ 156 = 110 + x ⇒ x = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Time = 6 hours

Speed for the first 2 hours = 60 m/s

Speed for the next 2 hours = 50 m/s

Speed for the remaining time = x m/s

Average speed for the entire journey = 52 m/s

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4618f54175c09a333679298b4d16b7d08661976ac6d78bceb71f39415f13cec6.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Remaining time for the last part of the journey = 6 − 2 − 2 = 2 hours

⇒ Since time acts directly as a weight in the average calculation, the unit conversion factor from hours to seconds cancels out in the numerator and denominator.

⇒ Average Speed = [(S₁ × T₁) + (S₂ × T₂) + (S₃ × T₃)] ÷ Total Time

⇒ 52 = [(60 × 2) + (50 × 2) + (x × 2)] ÷ 6

⇒ 52 = (120 + 100 + 2x) ÷ 6

⇒ 52 × 6 = 220 + 2x

⇒ 312 = 220 + 2x

⇒ 2x = 312 − 220

⇒ 2x = 92

⇒ x = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a journey is covered in equal time intervals at different speeds, the average speed is simply the arithmetic mean of those speeds: Sₐvg = (S₁ + S₂ + ... + Sₙ) ÷ n.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If equal distances are covered at different speeds, the average speed is the harmonic mean of the speeds. For exactly two equal distances, the formula is: Sₐvg = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

General Average Speed Formula

For any standard journey with varying times and distances, the average speed is universally calculated as the ratio of total distance to total time: Sₐvg = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

questions.question: At which temperature are Fahrenheit and Celsius equal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-40.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• At **- 40** Fahrenheit and Celsius are equal.
 
• The** Triple point** is the state at which **all three states of matter co-exist**.
 
• The triple point of water is** 273.16 K.**
 
• The normal temperature of a human body is **37°C or 98.6 °F.**

 

Concept__:

__
 
• Temperature: It is the measure of the degree of hotness and coldness of a body.
 
• The SI unit of temperature is Kelvin (K).

Fahrenheit and Celsius are measurements of temperature and are related to each other as follows:

C = (F - 32) × (5)/(9)

Where C is the temperature in Celsius and F is the temperature in Fahrenheit.

EXPLANATION__:

Since we need temperature in fahrenheit and celsius to be equal:

Now, let C = F = x

So,

x = (x - 32) × (5)/(9)

or, 9x = 5x – 160

or, 4x = -160

or, x = -40

Therefore, -40°C = -40°F

• The **pulmonary artery** carries **deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.**
 
• Veins carry blood towards the heart.
 
• Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
 
• *__**Trick to remember**__- Arteries goes....Veins Come.*

questions.question: Black Soil is NOT found in which State of India?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Black soil is found in the Deccan traps region.**__
 
• Sandy loam to clayey soil is found in Punjab.
 
• It is ideal for growing cotton. It is also known as regur soils.

 
 

 
 
Alluvial soils

 
 
 
 
• It a fine-grained fertile soil deposited by water flowing over flood plains or in river beds.
 
• Nitrogen is generally low, but potash, phosphoric acid, and alkalis are adequate.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Black soils

 
 
 
 
• The black soil in India is rich in metals such as Iron, Magnesium, and Aluminium.
 
• It is deficient in Nitrogen, Potassium, Phosphorous, and Humus.
 
• Black soil is of black color mainly due to its iron oxide content.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Laterite soils

 
 
 
 
• Laterite is a soil and rock type rich in iron and aluminum and is commonly considered to have formed in hot and wet tropical areas.
 
• Nearly all laterites are of rusty-red coloration, because of high iron oxide content.
 
• Laterite soils are rich in iron and aluminum but deficient in nitrogen and potassium.

questions.question: Which of the following relations is true?

options.text: GNP ≡ GDP / Net factor income from abroad
GNP ≡ GDP + Net factor income from abroad
GNP ≡ GDP ̶ Net factor income from abroad
GNP ≡ GDP × Net factor income from abroad

questions.solution:
__
 
• Gross National Product is the sum of the Gross Domestic Product and net factor income from abroad.
 
• **GNP ≡ GDP + Net factor income from abroad.**__
 
• Gross Domestic Product is the measure of all finished goods and services made within a country during a specific period.
 
• Net National Product is computed by deducting depreciation from the gross national product.
 
• NNP = GNP – Depreciation
 
• Gross national product(GNP) is the net amount of all the goods and services produced in a country in a given year(GDP) along with the income from abroad.
 
• GNP= GDP + Income from Abroad
